subject: Discovery recap + proposed cost levers for FinWell pilot
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Reyes <amelia@finwell.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap + proposed cost levers for FinWell pilot

Amelia — thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed, with a focus on the unit economics and where we can optimize during a short pilot.

Key pain points you shared
- Production latency spikes at peak business hours causing poor UX for loan pre-approval flows.
- Current inference spend has become unpredictable; finance wants a predictable pilot budget.
- Regulatory need to retain audit logs and control data residency.

Goals for the pilot (30-45 days suggested)
- Proof out latency SLO: 95th percentile under 300ms for short inference paths.
- Demonstrate 30%+ cost reduction relative to your current hosted endpoint by combining batching and caching.
- Deliver audit logs and VPC isolation for PII-sensitive traffic.

Cost/TCO levers we highlighted (high level)
- Model choice: smaller open model variant for the pre-qualification step, full model for final scoring. This hybrid reduces tokens served by ~35% in our estimate.
- Batching: use adaptive batching with a 20ms latency floor during non-peak hours to increase throughput and reduce per-token cost.
- KV/prefix caching: cache common leading prompts for repeated pre-qual checks to cut repeated token costs.
- Quantization: Q4/INT8 profile for the dedicated nodes in the pilot to reduce GPU memory needs and allow cheaper instance types.

Budget constraints you mentioned
- Target monthly pilot spend cap: about 18k USD.
- Procurement needs estimate and SOW by next Wednesday to start internal approvals.

Immediate next steps
1) I will send a short estimate workbook with two scenarios (conservative and optimized). Attachment: redwood_pilot_estimate_v2.xlsx
2) Lauren to align on SOW language and procurement routing.
3) Schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with your infra/security next week to confirm VPC and logging details.

If that aligns, I will mark out capacity for a 6-node dedicated pool for the pilot in our dedicated environment for the tentative dates 2026-12-01 to 2026-01-15.

Thanks again — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

From: Amelia Reyes <amelia@finwell.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finwell.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed cost levers for FinWell pilot

Vivek — thanks for the clear recap. That matches my notes. A few clarifications:
- The 18k/month cap is firm for the initial pilot; we may be able to stretch by another 5k if the cost model proves out.
- Peak concurrency during business hours is typically 120 concurrent sessions with median request size ~450 tokens and an occasional longer follow-up of ~1.2k tokens.
- Security: we need SOC2 evidence and confirmation that logs can be exported to our SIEM with a 90-day retention during the pilot period.

Please send the two-scenario workbook and a one-page SOW with the removal of beta feature clauses. Procurement needs the SOW by next Wednesday (2026-11-25) to route approvals.

Amelia
Director, AI Product
FinWell
amelia@finwell.ai

On a separate note, looping in procurement to keep them in the thread for timing.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Reyes <amelia@finwell.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + proposed cost levers for FinWell pilot

Amelia — attaching the workbook and one-pager SOW as discussed. Summary of the two cost scenarios below so procurement has something concise to react to.

Attachment highlights
- redwood_pilot_estimate_v2.xlsx: tabbed scenarios, assumptions, and per-token math.
- pilot-scope-one-pager.pdf: SOW summary, acceptance criteria, and timeline.

Scenario A (Conservative) — estimated monthly run rate: 17,900 USD
- Model: single mid-sized open model for both pre-qual and scoring
- Batching: conservative batching window (10ms), KV cache enabled for common prompts (~12% token reduction)
- Reserved dedicated nodes: 4 GPUs with baseline autoscaling for bursts
- Audit/log delivery: included via secure S3 export

Scenario B (Optimized) — estimated monthly run rate: 12,700 USD
- Hybrid model: small model for pre-qual (reduces tokens served by ~38%), large model only on final scoring
- Aggressive adaptive batching in off-peak windows (20-30ms floor) + warmed KV cache (~22% token reduction)
- Quantized runtime for pre-qual paths to reduce instance footprint

Key assumptions (please confirm)
- Average interaction length: 450 tokens; 12% of requests trigger the heavier 1.2k token flow.
- 30-day pilot with expected 120 concurrent peak sessions.
- We included a 10% buffer for traffic variance.

If FinWell confirms the assumptions, we can lock the Scenario B configuration and issue a pilot SOW for procurement by 2026-11-24.

Next actions
- Amelia: confirm buffer tolerance and SOC2 evidence channel (we can provide a SOC2 AICPA link and a redacted report for procurement).
- Procurement: review attached SOW; Vivek/LAuren available for any redlines.
- Internal: I will book a 30-minute security walkthrough with your infra on Mon 2026-11-23.

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_pilot_estimate_v2.xlsx (Excel)]
[Attachment: pilot-scope-one-pager.pdf (PDF)]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: FinWell pilot SOW and procurement timeline (quick)

Team — quick internal note after seeing Vivek's attachments. Procurement will almost certainly accept the one-pager but will push for the absolute monthly cap in the SOW. Two asks for us to be ready:
1) Stephanie: can you confirm feasibility of the 22% token reduction number from KV cache warmed states and the quantization profile for the pre-qual path? I want a short sentence we can include in the SOW about expected token savings and typical latency impact.
2) Vivek: hold the tentative dedicated pool for 2026-12-01 to 2027-01-15 as discussed; I'll start drafting the SOW with the hard cap and an opt-in clause for Scenario B if procurement approves.

I'll also queue Naomi to prep SOC2 evidence redaction if procurement requests it.

Thanks — Lauren
